messages:
maya: Weird inconsistency between JS and Python embeddings in the Next/LlamaIndex starter. JS vectors are sometimes ~10-20% different and the eval harness flags regressions.

julian: can you paste versions and repro? which embedder are you using?

maya: using @redwood/sdk-js@0.10.2, python-sdk 0.10.2 as well, model: text-embed-32k (open-embed-32k). Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/next-llamaindex-starter (branch: embed-parity). Steps: pnpm install && python -m venv && run the small script in /scripts/compare_embeddings.py

maya: script output snippet: 
```
JS mean cosine sim vs PY baselines: 0.78
PY mean cosine sim vs baseline: 0.96
JS diffs: 0.12, 0.09, 0.18, ...
```

rachel: that gap is huge. are you sure the same preprocessing/tokenization is used? JS pipeline might normalize whitespace differently.

maya: I also checked raw text and prompt. Using identical input strings. Token counts reported differ by 1-2 tokens in some examples.

sam: could be an embed streaming vs batch path parity bug. JS embedding uses streaming fallback when several items present (to save memory) and applies a final quantize step that python doesn't.

julian: open question: do both SDKs call the same model variant and same content-type header? sometimes JS uses application/json; charset=utf-8 which some infra treat differently.

maya: header dump: 
```
JS: Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
PY: Content-Type: application/json
Model-Name: open-embed-32k
```

maya: also saw a small rounding path in the JS path: Float32 -> Float16 conversion before L2 norm.

rachel: good find. even small numeric casts can cause larger cos sim deltas across many dims. but 0.78 vs 0.96 still surprising. suggestion: add an A/B where JS uses float32 full path (no downcast) and compare.

maya: ran that: enabling JS full-precision mode (env REDWOOD_EMBED_FP=fp32) raises mean sim to 0.94. so casting was the main offender.

sam: ok that's actionable. we should default to fp32 for small-batch demo pipelines and document the tradeoff (memory vs fidelity). also add a flag in the starter's env and the eval harness to avoid false positives.

julian: can we add a unit test in devex/eval-harness that compares embedding parity within a threshold and fails only if drift > 0.05? put it on main CI.

maya: I'm creating a small PR to the sample to set REDWOOD_EMBED_FP=fp32 in dev mode and add a note in README. PR will include a script to regenerate python baselines.

ci-bot: Issue created: RED-DEVEX-4211 "JS SDK embedding downcast causes eval drift in Next starter" (assignee: sam).

rachel: also ping sdk team to consider changing default for SDK to avoid surprise for new users. flagged for discussion in SDK sync. @derek FYI.

sam: will follow up. thanks for the clear repro and the env knob, maya. :rocket:

maya: added the failing test to devex/eval-harness and a small note in samples/README.md. Will link PR when ready.
